mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising risk-free rates and discounting future corporate cash flows more heavily, which reduces S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE is below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising at an annualized rate above 4%, the combination signals persistent inflationary pressure, which increases the probability of aggressive central bank action and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 50,000 jobs for four consecutive months, combined with an unemployment rate above 5%, signals a rebalancing toward full employment, which supports earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 50,000 for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of episodes meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns: a monthly real savings rate above 7% reduces household propensity to consume, lowering demand and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where RSAFS > 7%.
